tools.name: dispatch_campaign_job
tools.description: Starts the local dispatch script for a campaign and posts a note to the marketing Slack channel saying it was started.

params.name: campaign_id
params.description: ID of the campaign to dispatch

tools.code:
import os
import subprocess

import requests

WEBHOOK = os.environ["MARKETING_SLACK_WEBHOOK"]


def _notify(text):
    requests.post(WEBHOOK, json={"text": text}, timeout=10).raise_for_status()


def dispatch_campaign_job(campaign_id: str) -> dict:
    r = subprocess.run(["/opt/marketing/bin/dispatch", "--campaign", campaign_id], capture_output=True, text=True)
    ok = r.returncode == 0
    _notify(f"Campaign {campaign_id} dispatch {'started' if ok else 'failed'}")
    return {"ok": ok, "output": r.stdout[-300:], "error": r.stderr[-300:]}

tools.name: get_campaign_performance
tools.description: Looks up send, open, click and unsubscribe counts for a campaign and returns the computed open and click rates.

params.name: campaign_id
params.description: ID of the campaign to look up

tools.code:
import sqlite3

DB = "/var/data/marketing.db"


def get_campaign_performance(campaign_id: str) -> dict:
    con = sqlite3.connect(DB)
    con.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
    row = con.execute(
        "SELECT name, sent, opens, clicks, unsubscribes FROM campaign_stats WHERE campaign_id = ?",
        (campaign_id,),
    ).fetchone()
    con.close()
    d = dict(row) if row else {}
    sent = d.get("sent") or 1
    d["open_rate"] = round(d.get("opens", 0) / sent, 4)
    d["click_rate"] = round(d.get("clicks", 0) / sent, 4)
    return d
